caption:
20% to 16.7%. That is the slide in women's representation in India Inc leadership, and Business Today spent two investigations tracing where it happens.

The answer they landed on: the first promotion. Not the corner office. The rung where the criteria quietly change.

Up to that point you are measured on output. Delivery, accuracy, hours. Past it, you are measured on presence — how you hold a room, how you sound when challenged, what you do in the pause before you answer.

Nobody publishes that second rubric. Most people find out they were graded on it after the decision is made.

In command, bearing was trained the way marksmanship was trained. Deliberately. Under observation. Corrected until it held under pressure.

The skill is learnable. It was never a personality trait. It was drill.

If your work is landing and your name still isn't, you are not failing at the job. You are being evaluated on something you were never taught.

topic.title: India Inc women leaders slid from 20% to 16.7%
topic.angle: The "first promotion trap" is a literal restatement of the audience's problem: qualified and delivering, but stalled at the exact rung where evaluation shifts from output to presence.
topic.why_now: Business Today ran a two-part investigation — Sept 10 and a follow-up five days ago on Sept 23 — so the statistic is still actively circulating in professional commentary.

rationale: A stark numbers-only visual lets the statistic carry the weight without decoration, matching the plainspoken, command-brief tone of the caption.
